note: Per-mini listener-gate settings, read by scripts/glaeda-cmux-runner-hook from the release glaeda-update installed (docs/CMUX_MINI_RUNNER.md, 'Per-mini gate settings'). Keys under hosts are the short, lowercased hostname (hostname -s), not the manifest member name. cpuHold false: the CPU marks (85/80 over 60 s) never hold that mini's listeners; units, memory pressure, heat, disk and the fleet's holds still do. A host entry with an until (UTC) is ignored past it, so a trial ends by itself. overloadHold (on with or without the CPU hold; side and root runners only, as gui, session, freshness, nightly and gateway runners are exempt like the CPU hold): an idle listener stops while the 1-minute load is at least pausePerCore x cores and CPU busy is at least cpuAtLeast %, and listens again below resumePerCore x cores; false turns it off, per host as well. A hold past 30 min listens anyway until the load falls (GATE_LOAD_MAX_HOLD_S), so no label is stranded. hostLoadCap (cmuxterm-hq#12331's CMUX_CI_HOST_LOAD_CAP at the listener; side and root runners only, the same exemptions): a listener on a mini whose mean 1-minute load over 2 min is above hostLoadCap per core takes no new job while another host's listener keeps up with its label (the build controller's workflow_job feed), and listens the moment a job of its label waits 2 min, an urgent or pinned one queues, or the feed cannot say; a number, or false for off, by default or per host; CMUX_CI_HOST_LOAD_CAP in the runner's environment wins (off turns it off). 2026-11-16 23:5xZ: cmux21 ran at 6.4x its cores and cmux22 at 5.5x while other Macs idled. memoryCap (cmuxterm-hq#12838; every runner but the nightly, freshness, gateway and dedicated ones): an idle listener takes no new job while reclaimable memory (free, purgeable and file-backed pages) is under needGiB or memory pressure is 2 or more, and listens again at resumeGiB; it only defers, like hostLoadCap, and listens once a job of its label waits maxWaitMin, an urgent or pinned job queues, or the hold lasts maxWaitMin with no other listener known to keep up; true, false or a dict, by default or per host; GLAEDA_RUNNER_MEMORY_CAP=off in the runner's environment turns it off.

defaults.why: 2026-10-30 A/B (glaeda#1757): with the CPU hold off, 3 std minis started 15% more jobs per mini-hour than 3 matched controls (difference-in-differences against the 2 h before), with no rise in failures, no slower normalized p90 and shorter nightly waits. Units, memory pressure, heat, disk and the fleet's holds still gate every listener.

overloadHold.why: 2026-11-05 (Leo: "i meant can you do all of htem", research/2026-11-05-where-we-stand.md section 4, route by pressure): cmux8s-14 took jobs at loads 90-122 on 14 cores (cmux14 8.5 per core, 100% CPU, 13 of 14 units) while other Macs idled. Past twice the cores another job only slows the running ones; held off, the job goes to a mini with room or the overflow. The CPU must agree because the 09-28 load-only gate held 578 runner-hours at 34-59% CPU.

memoryCap.why: 2026-11-16/17 (Leo, 2026-11-05: "i meant can you do all of htem"; cmuxterm-hq#12838): the 16 GiB minis cmux17, 18, 21 and 22 showed the out-of-application-memory panel running 4-6 jobs; cmux17's 22:34Z JetsamEvent killed daemons for low swap while eight swift-frontend processes held 2.8-6.5 GiB each. A swift-frontend peaks near 4 GiB, so a new job waits for that much reclaimable memory while another host has room.

cmux16.why: Reserved for perf work until 20:50Z (the fleet registry's reservation, which lapses then): keeps the 85/80 CPU hold so this change does not move its measurements; the entry lapses with it, so move both together if the reservation is extended.
